_comment: Work item catalog. basis is what the quantity is measured in. Material quantity = quantity * multiplier / coverage * (1 + waste), summed per SKU and rounded up to whole purchase units. An item is one visit unless it has 'stages': then one selection in a scope becomes several visits, each with its own phase, hours, wait and materials (drywall coats, electrical rough-in and trim-out). An item 'note' is printed under ASSUMPTIONS whenever the item is in a scope.
_rates: hours_per_unit and setup_hours are SAMPLE production rates and are judgment values. The published labor guides (annual cost data books, trade association labor unit manuals) are paid publications that could not be opened for the source review in docs/assumptions.md, so no hours per unit figure here is confirmed by a source. They were later compared against planned hours in a handful of the author's own past estimates (docs/assumptions.md, 'Compared against the author's own estimates'): most lines agree, but those are planned hours from one or two estimates each, not tracked actuals, so the rates stay judgment. Replace them with your own crew's numbers.
_sources: Material coverage, fastener spacing, coat schedules, cure and dry times and the order of work were checked against manufacturer data sheets and gypsum industry documents. docs/assumptions.md lists each default as confirmed, corrected or judgment, with the source titles.

items.name: Frame walls on concrete slab
items.note: Walls on a slab: pressure treated bottom plate over sill sealer, pinned with concrete fasteners about every 32 inches and 6 inches from each plate end, then untreated studs and a double top plate. The residential code calls for treated wood where a plate sits on a slab in contact with the ground, unless a moisture barrier separates them. Evaluation reports for powder driven pins allow up to 3 or 4 ft between pins on interior non bearing walls. The sill sealer and the double top plate are judgment calls.

items.name: Set shower pan
items.note: The shower pan is set against the bare studs before any board goes up. The backer board then stops just above the pan's tile flange, as pan makers' instructions show.

items.name: Hang and finish ceiling drywall
note: Drywall is five visits: hang, tape coat, second coat, finish coat, sand. Tape plus two more coats on the flat joints is the Level 4 finish in the gypsum industry's levels of finish. Ceilings are hung before walls. Screws are 12 inches on center on ceilings and 16 on walls.

Drywall dry time: one dry day after each coat of premixed all purpose compound. That holds at about 60 to 70 F and 50 percent humidity with ventilation. The gypsum industry drying table gives about 17 hours at 70 F and 50 percent humidity, 24 hours at 60 F, 26 hours at 70 F and 70 percent, and 38 hours at 60 F and 70 percent, so allow two days a coat in a cool damp basement and keep the room at 50 F or warmer. Setting compound would shorten the wait.

Drywall materials per 1,000 sf of board: 10 gallons of premixed compound (one 4.5 gallon bucket per 450 sf across the three coats; published figures run 9 to 11 gallons), 370 ft of paper tape, 1,250 screws (one 5 lb box of 1-1/4 inch screws).

materials.note: 5 lb box, about 1,250 screws; a board maker's estimator gives 1,250 screws per 1,000 sf
250 ft roll at 370 ft of tape per 1,000 sf of board
tape coat is about 40 percent of the compound

items.name: Cement backer board
items.note: Backer board screws: coverage assumes a box of 185 screws, 1-1/4 inch, at the 8 inch spacing board makers call for. Walls take about 2 screws per sf (8 inches on center into studs at 16 inches), so one box covers about 90 sf. Floors take about 3.7 per sf (8 inches on center both ways, edges included), so one box covers about 50 sf. The spacing is the makers'; the screws per sf are worked out from it and sit at the high end. Seams are mesh taped and filled from the tile thinset.

materials.note: box of 185, about 2 screws per sf on walls
150 ft roll, about 0.55 ft of seam per sf of 3x5 board

items.name: Roll on waterproofing membrane
items.note: Roll on membrane: two coats over the taped cement board at about 50 sf per gallon for the finished membrane. Product data sheets give 40 to 55 sf per gallon and say rough board takes more. A coat dries in an hour or so at 70 F. The cure day before tile is the long end of what the data sheets ask before a flood test: 2 hours for one product at 70 F, 12 to 24 hours for another, a full day below 70 F.

materials.note: two coats, about 50 sf per gallon for the finished membrane

items.name: Tile shower walls
items.note: Tile is two visits: set, then grout after the mortar has cured for a day. Grout makers ask for 24 to 48 hours of mortar cure before grouting unless the mortar is rapid setting, and for 16 to 24 hours on the grout before it is walked on or disturbed, so a second day follows the grout. How the hours divide between setting and grouting is a judgment. Tile waste is 10 percent for a straight layout on a floor or backsplash and 12 percent on shower walls; use the waste override for a diagonal or herringbone layout (15 percent or more).

materials.note: two coats

items._rate: one prime coat and two finish coats, brush and roller, with the cut-in a small room needs; a judgment value
items.note: Paint on new drywall: one coat of drywall primer at 300 sf per gallon, then two finish coats at 350 sf per gallon. Paint and primer data sheets give 300 to 400 sf per gallon and the same one primer coat and two finish coats.

items.name: Floor tile underlayment, backer board
note: Floor tile underlayment default: 1/4 inch cement backer board bedded in thinset over a sound wood subfloor, screwed 8 inches on center, seams mesh taped and filled with thinset. The thinset bed, the 1/4 inch square notch trowel and the 8 inch screw spacing are the board makers' instructions. The board goes down after paint, right before the floor tile: that order is a judgment, since the makers' instructions do not set one. If you use an uncoupling membrane instead, swap this item for your own.

items.name: Prep concrete slab for tile
items.note: Tile on a concrete slab: no backer board. The slab is scraped clean and low spots and cracks are filled with patching compound before tile is bonded straight to it. Moisture testing and crack isolation membrane are not included.
